question: Is the closure-valid learned H3 axis reproducible and selectively necessary when removed from natural donor H3 states?

frozen_design.fit: repeat v1 exactly: even A1, rank1, empirical delta span, DIM plus seeds 1/2, 150 Adam steps at lr .03, normalized match+complement objective
frozen_design.artifact: store the selected unit-norm 128-vector and its canonical float32 byte SHA256
frozen_design.sufficiency_replay: repeat v1 heldout A1 and A2 subspace/complement arms
frozen_design.necessity: on each natural donor prompt, replace the learned H3 coefficient with its matched base coefficient and measure movement toward the base answer
frozen_design.controls: apply the same coefficient neutralization to natural donor P and C prompts and report normalized collateral

predictions.pred_a_exact_fit_reproduction: best objective, selected-start identity, span rank, and selected-axis projector reproduce v1 within 1e-6
predictions.pred_b_sufficiency_reproduction: heldout/A2 axis and complement fractions reproduce v1 within 0.01
predictions.pred_c_bidirectional_necessity: donor-axis neutralization moves toward base on >=0.75 of rows and recovers >=0.25 of the full native contrast in both A1-heldout and A2
predictions.pred_d_selective_neutralization: normalized P and C donor collateral are <=0.20 and <=0.35
predictions.pred_e_executable_axis_artifact: stored vector has exactly 128 finite float32 coordinates, norm within 1e-5 of one, and canonical byte hash agrees
predictions.pred_f_managed_price: registered forward/evaluation/backward/update ceilings are respected with no new rank, seed, or threshold search

terminal_rules.invalid: authority, deterministic reproduction, finiteness, artifact identity, or price fails
terminal_rules.sufficiency_only: A/B/D/E/F pass but bidirectional necessity fails
terminal_rules.null: valid reproduction but the axis is not selective or not transferable

interpretation_limits: This tests necessity of the H3 axis contribution, not necessity of the entire two-reader temporal circuit.
The axis is defined operationally in the fixed H3 coordinate system and is not a cross-layer vector.
No post-result rank increase or additional seed is licensed.
